Type.evidence_source: Data analysis was guided by constant comparison methods (Corbin & Strauss, 2008) wherein the first and third authors read the 35 hard copy interviews highlighting key excerpts and jotting notes in the margins to signal and share interpretations, and develop preliminary codes for organizing the data.

Area.evidence_source: Early on in the analyses, the overarching theme of social isolation was evident and six codes were labeled with descriptors to organize data underpinning this phenomena: (a) family, (b) school and work, (c) self-care, (d) health care, (e) an idealized identity, and (f) society. Data coded to each of the six codes were read to identify patterns and explore diversity in participant's experiences of social isolation and suicidality. Within each code, discrete findings were inductively derived to share what prevailed across participants. For example, data coded to family revealed dysfunction and estrangement as overarching in participants narratives about family-related social isolation.
